subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI cross-channel observe/mirror mode, and if so should the first supported shape be read-only and visibility-scoped rather than interactive bidirectional mirroring?
rationale: The requested feature crosses channel and session privacy boundaries and may add public CLI/config surface, so automation cannot choose the security policy or product shape safely.

options.title: Read-only scoped observe mode
options.body: Add an explicit `openclaw tui --observe` or equivalent opt-in that can display only sessions the current operator is authorized to see, with clear identity/session scope and live proof.

options.title: Interactive bidirectional mirror
options.body: Allow the TUI to both observe and send across mirrored channels, accepting a larger delivery, message-loss, and privacy-policy surface before implementation.

options.title: Keep logs as the workaround
options.body: Reject core observer/mirror mode for now and leave `openclaw logs --follow` plus explicit session selection as the supported monitoring path.

recommendation.title: Read-only scoped observe mode
recommendation.body: Add an explicit `openclaw tui --observe` or equivalent opt-in that can display only sessions the current operator is authorized to see, with clear identity/session scope and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They landed the session-isolation behavior and have recent TUI session lifecycle ownership signals, making them the best available decision owner from the inspected history.
